methods.label: Match each part of the trip
methods.explanation:
On a distance-from-home graph, traveling away from home makes the graph rise, traveling toward home makes it fall, and stopping makes it horizontal. Faster travel produces a steeper segment because the distance changes more in the same amount of time.

Mike first drives away slowly and then faster, so the graph must rise gently and then steeply. While he shops for an hour, his distance from home stays constant, giving a horizontal segment. He then returns quickly along the highway and slowly through the city, so the graph falls steeply and then gently until the distance reaches \(0\).

Graphs C, D, and E have no horizontal interval for shopping. Graph A has a shopping interval but does not show the changes between slow city travel and fast highway travel. Graph B shows all five parts in the correct order. The answer is \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
